description: Ed25519/X25519 public-key validity parity between spindle-core and @spindle/crypto (td-b8c68a). Rust's checked_verifying_key and TS's requireEd25519PublicKey must agree on every "ed25519" case; every "x25519" case is expected to ACCEPT on both sides (X25519 public keys are deliberately unvalidated beyond length -- see spindle_core::checked_verifying_key's doc comment).

cases.name: ed25519_not_a_curve_point
cases.description: 32 bytes, canonical range, but does not decompress to any Ed25519 curve point.

cases.name: ed25519_non_canonical_y_eq_18
cases.description: [0xff; 32]: the non-canonical encoding of y = 18 (p + 18, reduced mod 2^255). Bare VerifyingKey::from_bytes accepts this; checked_verifying_key (and noble's ed25519.Point.fromBytes) reject it -- the divergence td-b8c68a closes.

cases.name: ed25519_valid_derived_key
cases.description: A genuinely derived Ed25519 verifying key -- always canonically encoded.

cases.name: ed25519_identity_point_sign_bit_set
cases.description: y = 1, sign_bit = 1: the non-canonical encoding of the identity point (0, 1). RFC 8032 5.1.3's second canonicality rule (no 'negative zero' when x == 0) is violated. Bare VerifyingKey::from_bytes accepts this (dalek's conditional_negate has no x == 0 guard); checked_verifying_key (and noble's ed25519.Point.fromBytes) reject it.

cases.name: ed25519_order2_point_sign_bit_set
cases.description: y = p - 1, sign_bit = 1: the non-canonical encoding of the order-2 point (0, -1). Same rule as ed25519_identity_point_sign_bit_set, at the curve's other x == 0 point. Must be rejected.

cases.name: ed25519_order2_point_sign_bit_clear
cases.description: y = p - 1, sign_bit = 0: the *canonical* encoding of the same order-2 point (0 is never negative, so 0 is the correct sign bit). Must stay ACCEPTED -- pins that the sign-bit-set fix above does not overreach into rejecting this legitimate encoding.

cases.name: x25519_low_order_point_u_eq_1
cases.description: X25519 low-order point (u = 1). Deliberately ACCEPTED on both languages: X25519 public keys are unvalidated by design (x25519_dalek::PublicKey::from is infallible), and this pins that agreement rather than an oversight.
